name: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
add: Nandgram Dham: Kṛṣṇa Himself, with the mood and complexion of Śrī Rādhā (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 1.5; Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11). Called Viśvambhara, Nimāi, Gaurahari and Gaurāṅga, later Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. Sannyāsa at twenty-four at Kāṭoyā, from Keśava Bhāratī. He left this world on 14 June 1534 at Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha, Jagannātha Purī. His written legacy: the eight verses of the Śikṣāṣṭaka.

name: Dāmodara Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: the tenth branch of the Caitanya tree (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.31–32); his younger brother was Śaṅkara Paṇḍita, called the Lord's «foot-pillow». He kept etiquette and discipline in the Lord's circle, in Purī and later in Navadvīpa. Best-known episode: he rebuked the Lord for His affection for a widowed brāhmaṇī's son, and in reward was sent to Navadvīpa (to look after Śacīmātā). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Devakīnandana dāsa
add: Nandgram Dham: disciple of Puruṣottama dāsa Ṭhākura, a close associate of Nityānanda Prabhu; his godbrothers Mādhavācārya (Mādhava Caṭṭopādhyāya) and Yādavācārya were also brāhmaṇa disciples of Puruṣottama Ṭhākura. He wrote the Vaiṣṇava-vandanā, with the closing prayer «Vaiṣṇava-śaraṇa» that is still sung; two songs signed with his name survive in the Vaiṣṇava songbook. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Devānanda Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: his home and school were at Kuliyā, near the house of Maheśvara Viśārada, the father of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; a professional reciter and teacher of the Bhāgavatam, trained in Nyāya. As Bhāguri Muni he was the chief paṇḍita in Nanda Mahārāja's court.

name: Dhanañjaya Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: the sixteenth of Nityānanda Prabhu's chief branches in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta. His śrīpāṭa is Śītala-grāma, Maṅgalkoṭ (Burdwan), where he installed Śrī Gopīnātha, Śrī Nitāi-Gaurāṅga and a Dāmodara śālagrāma-śilā. His wife Haripriyā is named only by later sources, not by the Caitanya-caritāmṛta.

name: Gadādhara dāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: his known disciple was Yadunandana Cakravartī of Kāṭoyā; Nandgram Dham keeps his disappearance on the bright (śukla) aṣṭamī of Kārtika.

name: Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: born around 1486, the same year as Mahāprabhu, at Navadvīpa, of a family from Chittagong; the bhakta-śakti of the Pañca-tattva (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11, 147; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.15).

name: Gaṅgā Dāsa Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: his home and school were at Gaṅgānagara, in Sīmantadvīpa near Navadvīpa; he taught grammar and scripture to young Nimāi, a teacher, not a dīkṣā guru. Vasiṣṭha Muni appeared by a special manifestation as both Gaṅgādāsa and Sudarśana (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 53). The earliest source is the Caitanya-bhāgavata.

name: Gaṅgānārāyaṇa Cakravartī
add: Nandgram Dham: he was with Narottama Ṭhākura in his last days at Gambhilā. His descendants keep the Baḍo Govinda Bāḍī at Śrīpāṭ Gambhilā, Jiaganj (Murshidabad). Where his samādhi is, is disputed.

name: Śrī Gaṅgāmātā Gosvāminī
add: Nandgram Dham: born Śacī Devī (not the mother of Śrī Caitanya) at Puṭiyā (Puthia), Rajshahi; her father, the zamindar-rāja Nareśa Nārāyaṇa, is said to have become a Vaiṣṇava through Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's preaching. Her guru Haridāsa Paṇḍita was the chief pūjārī of Rādhā-Govinda in Vṛndāvana: Gadādhara Paṇḍita → Ananta Ācārya → Haridāsa Paṇḍita, the one line of the great Gauḍīya women that the Caitanya-caritāmṛta names directly (Ādi 8.60). She took kṣetra-sannyāsa, the vow never to leave Purī. Dates c. 1601–1721 by the Gaṅgāmātā Maṭha's own record.

name: Śrīla Gaura Kiśora Dāsa Bābājī
add: Nandgram Dham: born on 17 November 1838 at Vāgyāna near Ṭepākholā, Faridpur district (now Bangladesh), of a merchant family (sources differ on how rich and on the trade). He left home after his wife's death, in his late twenties. Who gave him the bābājī vows is disputed between the sources.

name: Śrī Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: son of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, a Śrī Vaiṣṇava priest of the Śrī Raṅganātha temple; formally initiated by his uncle Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī, and taken as a younger brother by Rūpa and Sanātana in Vṛndāvana. He edited the Hari-bhakti-vilāsa and wrote the Sat-kriyā-sāra-dīpikā and a commentary on the Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta. Born c. 1503, left this world traditionally in 1578, in Vṛndāvana, at about seventy-five.

name: Śrī Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: the Lord gave him the title «Guru» jokingly when he was a boy in Purī. His foremost disciple was Śrī Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī.
